mainEntity.name: How do you calculate the cost per delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add the driver, the fuel and the truck for one day, then divide by the stops. A $28.00 driver over 8 hours is $224.00, 120 miles at 8 mpg is $61.50 of fuel at $4.10, and the truck day is $95.00. That $380.50 across 14 drops is $27.18 a delivery.

mainEntity.name: Where should a delivery minimum be set?

acceptedAnswer.text: Above the margin a stop has to earn, not at a round number. At $27.18 a drop, an account buying at a 20% margin has to order $135.90 of product before the stop pays for itself. Set the minimum so the smallest order on the truck still clears that.

mainEntity.name: Should you charge customers for delivery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Either charge for it or price it in, but do it knowing the number. At $0.54 a case, a 50 case drop absorbs the stop without anyone noticing. At $2.72 a case, a 10 case drop does not, so that is where a delivery charge or a minimum belongs.

mainEntity.name: What does a light drop do to your margin?

acceptedAnswer.text: It takes it a case at a time. The same $27.18 stop spread over 10 cases is $2.72 a case against a $0.91 route average. If the gross margin on those cases is under $2.72, the delivery costs more than the order earns.

mainEntity.name: Should you drop an account that orders too little?

acceptedAnswer.text: Change the frequency or the minimum before you drop it. An account taking a stop every week at 10 cases can take one every other week at 20 cases, and the route cost falls from $2.72 a case to $1.36 with the same volume sold.

mainEntity.name: How do you count the truck's fixed cost in a delivery cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: As a cost per route day, not a cost per mile. Take the lease or depreciation, insurance, maintenance and plates for the year, then divide by the days the truck actually runs. At $95.00 a day that is 25.0% of a $380.50 route before the truck leaves the yard.

mainEntity.name: What is the cost per case on a delivery route?

acceptedAnswer.text: Route cost over the cases that route carries. $380.50 across 420 cases is $0.91 a case, and $3.17 a mile across 120 miles. Load 840 cases on the same day and the case cost falls to $0.45, while the cost per drop stays at $27.18.
